subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Does the linked PR's stable model-visible tool catalogue, paired with immutable pre-hook and pre-side-effect runtime authorization, preserve the intended OpenClaw security boundary across core tools, plugin tools, and gateway MCP execution?
rationale: The implementation is source-complete and well-proven, but accepting model-visible schemas that are not executable on the current turn is an intentional security architecture choice requiring owner confirmation.

options.title: Approve unified policy boundary
options.body: Accept the stable catalogue plus immutable execution policy after refreshing the PR against current main and confirming all protected paths use the canonical denial wrapper.

options.title: Require narrower visibility
options.body: Request a revised contract that hides unavailable schemas, accepting reduced prompt-cache continuity to retain visibility-as-authority semantics.

options.title: Pause the candidate
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers design a different durable authorization and prompt-cache contract.

recommendation.title: Approve unified policy boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the stable catalogue plus immutable execution policy after refreshing the PR against current main and confirming all protected paths use the canonical denial wrapper.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties the central agent, gateway, and Codex runtime surfaces to this owner, making them the best available decision point for the cross-boundary security contract.
